t: Dante wrote of the Redemption of humanity in the vernacular rather than the Latin one might expect, and the poem helped establish Tuscan as the standardized Italian language.
Its realms follow a pattern of nine plus one and its verse a pattern of threes, and its thought draws on Aristotle, Thomas Aquinas and the Vulgate, while Dante's exile from Florence runs through it.

It has one of the most extensive critical traditions of any work of literature, with line-by-line commentaries across Europe, the Americas and Asia, and it has been translated into English more times than into any other language.
dyk: Each of the three cantiche ends on the same word, stelle (“stars”), and each tercet of terza rima has 33 syllables, the number of cantos in each cantica.
ev: Dante is exiled from Florence with the White Guelphs, an exile that lasts the rest of his life
Dante completes the poem shortly before his death
Giovanni Boccaccio's Trattatello in laude di Dante gives the earliest known use of the adjective Divina for the poem
Giovanni da Serravalle makes the first complete translation, into Latin prose, during the Council of Constance
The first printed edition is published in Foligno; fourteen of its 300 copies survive
Lodovico Dolce's edition, published by Gabriele Giolito de' Ferrari, is the first to call the poem Divina Comedia in its title
Miguel Asín Palacios argues for Islamic sources of the poem in La Escatología musulmana en la Divina Comedia

f.made: Dante Alighieri, a White Guelph exiled from Florence in 1302, who began it about 1308 and completed it about 1321, shortly before his death
f.form: Narrative poem in Tuscan of 14,233 lines of eleven syllables in terza rima, in three cantiche, Inferno, Purgatorio and Paradiso, of 33 cantos each, with an opening canto making 100
f.where: No manuscript in Dante's hand survives; the Italian Dante Society lists some 800 manuscript copies of the 14th and 15th centuries, and fourteen of the 300 copies of the first printed edition (Foligno, 1472) survive
f.known: the nine circles of Hell; the contrapasso, punishment that fits the sin; Virgil, Beatrice and Bernard of Clairvaux as guides; Mount Purgatory; terza rima; “Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita”; its part in forming standard Italian
